title: Suno Announces Adding Watermarks to AI Songs and Signing Copyright Detection Agreement

content_html:
AI music generation platform Suno has announced a series of new measures today, including adding watermark marks to tracks generated on the platform, restricting downloads, and updating community guidelines to prevent counterfeit songs. These changes come as Suno faces multiple lawsuits from record companies and artist groups.

Co-founder and CEO Mikey Shulman outlined the platform's core principles in a blog post, stating that Suno aims to promote original creation while making its AI tools more accessible for people to create music.

A key point of contention is users uploading AI-generated songs to other streaming platforms and profiting from them. Suno says it will use audio watermarks and fingerprinting technology to prevent misuse on other platforms. It remains unclear whether Suno will adopt existing systems like Google Synth ID or develop its own solution, and TechCrunch has not received a response from the company on this issue.

In addition, Suno has reached an agreement with lyrics service Musixmatch to use its Sentinel system for copyright detection. Shulman wrote in the blog: "These tools are designed to be durable and tamper-resistant while not affecting the listening experience. They also do not intend to judge whether a song is good, meaningful, or human enough. Ultimately, we believe it should be up to artists and platforms to decide what to disclose, and our role is to provide transparent tools and encourage industry collaboration."

Suno also plans to introduce new download policies, prohibiting mass distribution on streaming platforms, but has refused to provide specific details.

Regarding community guidelines, Suno has clearly prohibited "falsely presenting fake audio as authentic content" and "using real people's voices or likenesses without permission" to prevent counterfeiting.

The company recently completed a $400 million Series D funding round, but legal battles have already begun. Suno is facing litigation with Universal Music Group (UMG) and Sony Music Group, coordinated by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). At the end of last month, a German court ruled in favor of the government-authorized copyright management body GEMA, finding Suno in violation of copyright rules.

content_html_zh:
AI音乐生成平台Suno今天宣布了一系列新措施，包括为平台生成的曲目添加水印、限制下载以及更新社区指南以防止假冒歌曲。 这些变化发生之际，Suno 面临着唱片公司和艺术家团体的多起诉讼。

联合创始人兼首席执行官 Mikey Shulman 在一篇博文中概述了该平台的核心原则，表示 Suno 的目标是促进原创创作，同时让人们更容易使用其人工智能工具来创作音乐。

争论的一个关键点是用户将人工智能生成的歌曲上传到其他流媒体平台并从中获利。 Suno 表示将使用音频水印和​​指纹识别技术来防止在其他平台上的滥用。 目前尚不清楚 Suno 是否会采用 Google Synth ID 等现有系统或开发自己的解决方案，TechCrunch 尚未收到该公司对此问题的回应。

此外，Suno还与歌词服务Musixmatch达成协议，使用其Sentinel系统进行版权检测。 舒尔曼在博客中写道：“这些工具被设计为耐用且防篡改，同时不会影响聆听体验。 他们也无意判断一首歌是否好听、是否有意义、是否足够人性化。 最终，我们认为应该由艺术家和平台来决定披露哪些内容，我们的作用是提供透明的工具并鼓励行业合作。”

Suno还计划推出新的下载政策，禁止在流媒体平台上大规模分发，但拒绝提供具体细节。

在社区准则方面，Suno明确禁止“以虚假音频冒充真实内容”和“未经许可使用真人的声音或肖像”，以防止假冒。

该公司最近完成了 4 亿美元的 D 轮融资，但法律诉讼已经开始。 Suno 正面临由美国唱片工业协会 (RIAA) 协调的环球音乐集团 (UMG) 和索尼音乐集团的诉讼。 上月底，德国一家法院做出了有利于政府授权版权管理机构 GEMA 的裁决，认定 Suno 违反了版权规则。
